title: Triangle Centers
blurb: The centroid, circumcenter, incenter and orthocenter, then the Euler line, the nine-point circle and some less famous centers. Midpoint, Perpendicular and Angle bisector come ready to hand.

items.title: Centroid
items.text:
Construct the centroid $G$ of triangle $ABC$, where its three medians meet. Each median joins a corner to the midpoint of the opposite side.

::: Hint
Two medians are enough: the third goes through the same point.
:::

items.title: Circumcenter
items.text:
Construct the circumcenter $O$ of triangle $ABC$: the point the same distance from all three corners, and so the center of the circle through them.

::: Hint
Every point on the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ is as far from $A$ as from $B$.
:::

items.title: Incenter
items.text:
Construct the incenter $I$ of triangle $ABC$: the point the same distance from all three sides, and so the center of the circle that touches them all.

::: Hint
Every point on the bisector of an angle is as far from one side as from the other.
:::

items.title: Orthocenter
items.text:
Construct the orthocenter $H$ of triangle $ABC$, where its three altitudes meet. Each altitude runs from a corner to the opposite side, at right angles to it.

::: Hint
Perpendicular draws an altitude in one step.
:::

items.title: Euler Line
items.text:
Construct the Euler line of triangle $ABC$, through its circumcenter and orthocenter. The centroid is on it too, a third of the way from the circumcenter to the orthocenter.

::: Hint
You’ve made tools for two of the points on it.
:::

items.title: Nine-Point Circle
items.text:
Construct the nine-point circle of triangle $ABC$. It passes through the midpoints of the three sides, the feet of the three altitudes, and the points halfway from each corner to the orthocenter.

::: Hint
Three of those nine points are enough, and some are easier to find than others.
:::

::: Hint
Your Circumcenter tool works on any three points.
:::

items.title: Excenter
items.text:
Construct the excenter $J$ of triangle $ABC$ opposite $A$: the center of the circle outside the triangle that touches side $BC$ and the extensions of $AB$ and $AC$.

::: Hint
$J$ is as far from line $AB$ as from line $BC$, and as far from line $AC$ as from line $BC$.
:::

::: Hint
The bisector of the angle outside the triangle at $B$ is perpendicular to the one inside it.
:::

items.title: Gergonne Point
items.text:
The incircle touches each side once. The lines joining each corner to where the incircle touches the opposite side meet at one point, the Gergonne point. Construct it.

::: Hint
The incircle touches a side where the perpendicular from its center meets it.
:::

items.title: Fermat Point
items.text:
Build an equilateral triangle outward on each side of $ABC$. The lines joining each new corner to the opposite corner of $ABC$ meet at one point, the Fermat point: the point whose distances to $A$, $B$ and $C$ add up to the least. Construct it.

::: Hint
The new corner on $BC$ is where two circles meet, on the far side of $BC$ from $A$.
:::

items.title: Symmedian Point
items.text:
Reflect each median of triangle $ABC$ across the angle bisector at the same corner. The three reflected lines meet at one point, the symmedian point. Construct it.

::: Hint
To reflect a line through $A$ across another line through $A$, reflect one other point of it.
:::

::: Hint
To reflect a point across a line, drop a perpendicular to the line and go as far again on the other side.
:::

items.title: Feuerbach Point
items.text:
The nine-point circle of triangle $ABC$ touches its incircle, at one point: the Feuerbach point. Construct it.

::: Hint
Two circles that touch do so on the line through their centers.
:::
